If someone steals an ox or a sheep and slaughters it or sells it, he shall pay five oxen for the ox and four sheep for the sheep.
If a thief is found breaking in and is struck and dies, it shall not count as murder for the one who struck him.
But if the sun has risen upon him, he is liable to death and shall die in return. But if he has nothing, he shall be sold to pay for his theft.
If he is caught and the stolen animal is found in his possession, whether an ox, a donkey, or a sheep, he shall pay double.

If someone grazes a field or a vineyard and lets his flock graze another person's field, he shall pay compensation from his own field according to its yield. But if he grazes the entire field, he shall pay compensation from the best part of his own field and the best of his own vineyard.
If a fire breaks out and reaches thorns, and along with them burns a threshing floor, a stack of sheaves, or a field, the one who started the fire shall pay full compensation.
If someone gives his neighbor silver or any other possession of his for safekeeping, and it is stolen from the man's house, then, if the thief is found, he shall repay double.
But if the thief is not found, the owner of the house shall come before God and swear that he himself has not in any way dealt dishonestly with his neighbor's deposit.

In every case of wrongdoing involving an ox, a donkey, a sheep, clothing, or anything lost, whatever the accusation of wrongdoing may concern, the case of both parties shall come before God. Whichever of them is found guilty by God shall repay his neighbor double.
If someone gives his neighbor a donkey, an ox, a sheep, or any other animal for safekeeping, and it is injured, dies, or is carried off, and no one knows about it,
Let there be an oath by God between the two, that he has not dealt deceitfully in any way with what his neighbor entrusted to him. Then its owner shall accept it, and he shall not pay compensation.
but if it is stolen from him, he shall make restitution to its owner.
But if it is torn by a wild animal, he shall bring a witness to the carcass and shall not make restitution.
If someone borrows an item from his neighbor, and it is broken, dies, or is carried off, and its owner is not with it, he shall certainly make restitution.
But if its owner is with it, he shall not make restitution. If it was hired, it shall be his in return for its hire.
If someone seduces a virgin who is not betrothed and sleeps with her, he shall pay the bride-price for her to be his wife.
If her father will not agree to give her to him as his wife, he shall pay silver to her father equal to the bride-price for virgins.
You shall not allow sorcerers to live.
You shall put to death anyone who has sexual relations with an animal.
Anyone who sacrifices to gods, except to the Lord alone, shall be destroyed.
You shall not mistreat a foreigner or oppress him, for you too were foreigners in the land of the Egyptians.
You shall not mistreat any widow or orphan.
But if you do mistreat them, and they raise a complaint and cry out to me, I will surely hear their cry.
I will become fiercely angry and kill you with the sword, and your wives shall become widows and your children orphans.
If you lend silver to your brother who is poor among you, you shall not press him for payment or charge him interest.
If you take your neighbor's cloak as a pledge, you shall return it before sunset.
For it is his covering, and it is the garment that covers his nakedness, in which he sleeps. If he cries out to me, I will hear him, for I am merciful.
You shall not revile your gods or curse the ruler of your people.
You shall not withhold the produce of your threshing floor and your winepress. You shall give me the firstborn of your sons.
You shall do the same with your ox, your sheep, and your donkey: it shall remain with its mother for seven days, and on the eighth day you shall give it to me.
You shall be holy people to me. You shall not eat the flesh of an animal torn by wild beasts in the open country, but shall throw it to the dogs.
You shall not accept a false report. You shall not agree with an unjust person to become an unjust witness.
You shall not willingly follow the many in doing evil. You shall not join a crowd and side with the many to pervert justice.
Do not show partiality to the poor in a lawsuit.
If you come upon your enemy’s ox or donkey wandering astray, bring it back and return it to him.
If you see your neighbor’s beast of burden fallen under its load, do not pass it by, but help him raise it.
Do not deny the poor justice in their lawsuits.
Keep away from every false matter. Do not kill the innocent or the righteous, and do not let the wicked live in exchange for a bribe.
Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds the eyes of those who see clearly and corrupts just words.
Do not oppress the foreigner, for you know how foreigners feel, since you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.
For six years you shall sow your land and gather its produce.

But in the seventh year you shall leave it alone and let it rest, so that the poor of your people may eat, and the wild animals may eat what they leave. Do the same with your vineyard and your olive trees.
For six days you shall do your work, but on the seventh day your ox and your donkey shall rest, and your maidservant’s son and the foreigner shall rest.
Keep everything that I have told you. Do not mention the names of foreign gods, and do not let them be heard from your mouth.
Three times a year you shall celebrate festivals for me.

You shall keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at the appointed time in the month of the early crops, for in that month you came out of the land of Egypt. You shall not appear before me empty-handed.

Celebrate the summer festival of the firstfruits of your produce, from the work you have cultivated in your field, and the festival at the end of the year, when you gather the produce of your work from the field.
Three times a year every male among you shall appear before the Lord God.
Do not offer the blood of your sacrifices with leavened bread, and do not let the fat of my festival offering remain overnight until morning.
Bring the first fruits of your harvest to the house of the Lord your God. Do not cook a lamb in its mother’s milk.
Look, I am sending my angel ahead of you to guard you on the way and bring you to the land that I have prepared for you.
Be on your guard and listen to him. Do not disobey him, for he will not give way to you, because my name is upon him.
If you truly listen to my voice and do everything I have told you, I will be an enemy to your enemies and stand against your adversaries.
For my angel will go ahead of you and bring you to the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites, and I will destroy them.
Do not bow down to their gods or serve them, and do not follow their practices. Instead, utterly demolish them and smash their pillars to pieces.
You shall serve the Lord your God, and I will bless your bread and your water and remove sickness from among you.
No one in your land shall be childless or barren. I will give you the full number of your days.
I will send my terror ahead of you and terrify every nation you enter, and I will make all your adversaries flee.
I will send hornets ahead of you, and they will drive the Amorites, Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites away from you.
I will not drive them away from you in a single year, so that the land does not become deserted and the wild animals of the land do not multiply against you.
Little by little I will drive them out before you, until you grow in number and inherit the land.

I will set your boundaries from the Red Sea to the sea of the Philistines, and from the wilderness to the great river Euphrates. I will deliver the inhabitants of the land into your hands and drive them out before you.
You must not make a covenant with them or with their gods.
They must not live in your land, lest they cause you to sin against me. For if you serve their gods, they will become a snare to you.
He said to Moses, “Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy men from the elders of Israel, and let them worship the Lord from a distance.”
Moses alone shall approach God; the others must not approach, and the people must not go up with them.
Moses came and told the people all the words of God and all the ordinances. All the people answered with one voice and said, “We will do and obey all the words that the Lord has spoken.”
Moses wrote down all the words of the Lord. Rising early in the morning, Moses built an altar at the foot of the mountain and set up twelve stones, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel.
He sent young men from the Israelites, and they offered burnt offerings and sacrificed calves as peace offerings to God.
Moses took half the blood and put it into bowls, and he poured out half the blood in front of the altar.
He took the book of the covenant and read it aloud to the people. They said, “We will do and obey everything that the Lord has spoken.”
Moses took the blood and sprinkled it on the people, saying, “Here is the blood of the covenant that the Lord has made with you concerning all these words.”
Moses and Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel went up.
They saw the place where the God of Israel stood. Beneath his feet was something like a pavement of sapphire bricks, as clear as the expanse of heaven.
Not one of the chosen men of Israel perished. They appeared in the place of God, and they ate and drank.
The Lord said to Moses, “Come up to me on the mountain and remain there. I will give you stone tablets and the law and commandments that I have written to instruct them.”
Moses and Joshua his attendant arose and went up the mountain of God.
He said to the elders, “Wait here until we return to you. Aaron and Hur are here with you; if anyone has a legal dispute, let them go to them.”
Moses went up the mountain, and the cloud covered the mountain.
The glory of God descended on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day the Lord called Moses from within the cloud.
The appearance of the Lord’s glory was like a blazing fire on the summit of the mountain, in the sight of the children of Israel.
Moses entered the cloud and went up the mountain. Moses was there on the mountain for forty days and forty nights.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Speak to the Israelites, and take an offering for me from those who are willing in their hearts. You shall receive my offerings.
This is the offering that you shall receive from them: gold, silver, and bronze;
blue, purple, and double-dyed scarlet yarn, spun fine linen, and goats’ hair;
rams’ skins dyed red, skins dyed blue, and wood that does not decay.
And oil for lighting, and spices for the anointing oil and for the incense mixture.
And sardius stones and stones for engraving, for the work of the ephod and the breastplate.
And you shall make me a sanctuary, and I will appear among you.
And you shall make it for me according to everything I showed you on the mountain—the pattern of the tabernacle and the pattern of all its furnishings. You shall make it this way.
You shall make an ark of the testimony from decay-resistant wood, two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one and a half cubits high.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold; you shall coat it inside and outside, and make a gold molding around it.
And you shall cast four gold rings for it and put them at its four corners, two rings on one side and two rings on the other side.
And you shall make poles from decay-resistant wood and overlay them with gold.
Insert the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark, to carry the ark with them.
For the poles shall remain in the rings of the ark of the covenant, without being moved from it.
And you shall put into the ark the testimony that I will give you.
And you shall make the atonement cover, an incense holder, from pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
And you shall make two cherubim of hammered gold and place them at the two ends of the atonement cover.
And the cherubim shall be one at one end and one at the other end of the atonement cover. You shall make two cherubim at its two ends.

And the cherubim shall spread their wings upward and shelter the atonement cover with their wings. Their faces shall face one another, so that the faces of the cherubim look toward the atonement cover.
And you shall put the atonement cover on top of the ark, and there in the ark you shall put the testimony that I will give you.

And I will reveal myself to you there and speak with you from above the atonement cover, from between the two cherubim that are on the ark of the testimony, concerning everything I commanded you for the children of Israel.
And you shall make a table from decay-resistant wood, two cubits long, one cubit wide, and one and a half cubits high.
And you shall overlay it with pure gold and make a gold molding all around it.
And you shall make a rim a handbreadth wide all around it, and make a molding all around the rim.
And you shall make four gold rings for it and put the rings at the four corners by its four legs, beneath the rim.
And the rings shall serve as holders for the poles with which to carry the table.
And you shall make the poles from decay-resistant wood and overlay them with pure gold, and the table shall be carried with them.
And you shall make its incense bowls and its boxes, its cups and its offering vessels, with which you shall make offerings. You shall make these from pure gold.
And you shall place bread on the table of the bread of the Presence, before me continually.
And you shall make a lampstand from pure gold. You shall make the lampstand of hammered work; its stem, branches, cups, knobs, and lilies shall be of one piece with it.
Six branches shall extend from its sides: three branches of the lampstand from one side and three branches of the lampstand from the other side.

And on one branch there shall be three cups fashioned with nut-shaped decorations, a knob, and a lily; and on the other branch three cups fashioned with nut-shaped decorations, a knob, and a lily. It shall be the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
And on the lampstand itself there shall be four cups fashioned with nut-shaped decorations, with its knobs and lilies.

There shall be a knob beneath two branches, made from the lampstand itself, and a knob beneath another two branches, made from the lampstand itself. You shall do the same for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
Their knobs and branches shall be made from the lampstand itself, all of turned work, from a single piece of pure gold.
And you shall make seven lamps for it and place the lamps on the lampstand, and they shall give light on one side, in front of it.
And you shall make its tongs and its supports of pure gold. You shall make all these utensils from one talent of pure gold.
Be careful to make it according to the pattern shown to you on the mountain.
And you shall make a tabernacle of ten curtains, of finely spun linen, blue, purple, and double-dyed scarlet. You shall make them with cherubim, the work of a weaver.
The length of one curtain shall be twenty-eight cubits, and the width of one curtain four cubits. All the curtains shall have the same measurements.
Five curtains shall be joined to one another, and the other five shall likewise be joined to one another.
And you shall make blue loops along the edge of one curtain, on the side where the sets are joined. You shall do the same along the outer edge of the curtain in the second set.
You shall make fifty loops on one curtain, and fifty loops along the side of the curtain belonging to the second set. The loops shall meet one another, each opposite its counterpart.
And you shall make fifty gold rings and join the curtains to one another with the rings, so that the tabernacle shall be one.
And you shall make upper curtains of haircloth as a covering for the tabernacle. You shall make eleven curtains.
The length of one curtain shall be thirty cubits, and the width of one curtain four cubits. All eleven curtains shall have the same measurements.
And you shall join the five curtains together in one set and the six curtains together in another set, and fold the sixth curtain double at the front of the tabernacle.
And you shall make fifty loops along the edge of one curtain at the joining, and fifty loops along the edge of the curtain in the second set.
And you shall make fifty bronze rings, connect the rings to the loops, and join the curtains so that they shall be one.
And you shall place the excess of the curtains beneath the tabernacle. With the remaining half of the extra curtain you shall cover the hanging portions of the tabernacle’s curtains at the back.
A cubit on this side and a cubit on that side, from the excess length of the tabernacle’s curtains, shall cover the sides of the tabernacle on either side.
And you shall make coverings for the tabernacle from rams’ skins dyed scarlet, and coverings of blue skins over them.
And you shall make upright posts for the tabernacle from decay-resistant wood.
You shall make the length of each post ten cubits, and the thickness and width of each post one and a half cubits.
And each post shall have two tenons fitted to one another. You shall make all the posts of the tabernacle this way.
And you shall make twenty posts for the north side of the tabernacle.
And you shall make forty silver bases for the twenty pillars: two bases for each pillar on its two sides, and two bases for each pillar on its two sides of the tabernacle.
And on the second side of the tabernacle, toward the south, there shall be twenty pillars,
and their forty silver bases, two bases for each pillar on its two sides.
And at the back of the tabernacle, toward the west, you shall make six pillars.
Make two pillars for the corners of the tabernacle on its rear side.
And they shall be joined together below, and likewise their capitals shall be paired in a single joint. You shall make the uprights for both corners in the same way.
And there shall be eight pillars and their silver bases, sixteen bases: two bases for each pillar on its two sides, and two bases for the next pillar as well.
And you shall make bars of rot-resistant wood, five bars for one pillar on one side of the tabernacle,
and five bars for another pillar on the second side of the tabernacle, and five bars for one pillar at the back of the tabernacle, toward the west.
And one bar in the middle of the pillars shall pass through from one side to the other.
And you shall cover the pillars with gold and make gold rings into which you shall fit the bars, and you shall cover the bars with gold.
And you shall erect the tabernacle according to the pattern shown to you there on the mountain.
And you shall make a curtain of blue and purple and spun scarlet yarn and woven fine linen. You shall make it as skilled woven work, with a cherub.
And you shall place it upon the four pillars of rot-resistant wood covered with gold; their capitals shall be gold and their bases silver.
And you shall stretch the curtain from pillar to pillar and bring the ark of the testimony inside the curtain. The curtain shall separate the Holy Place from the Holy of Holies for you.
And you shall cover the ark of the testimony with the curtain in the Holy of Holies.
And you shall place the table outside the curtain, and the lampstand opposite the table on the south side of the tabernacle; and you shall place the table on the north side of the tabernacle.
And you shall make a screen for the entrance of the tabernacle of blue and purple and spun scarlet yarn and woven fine linen, patterned work.
And you shall make five small pillars of rot-resistant wood for the curtain and coat them with gold. Their capitals shall be gold, and you shall cast five bronze bases for them.
And you shall make an altar of rot-resistant wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide. The altar shall be square, and its height shall be three cubits.
And you shall make its horns on its four corners, so that the horns are formed from the altar itself, and you shall cover it with bronze.
And you shall make the rim of the altar and its cover, its basins, its meat forks, and its firepans; and you shall make all its utensils of bronze.
And you shall make a bronze framework for it in the form of a grating, and you shall make four bronze rings for the framework on its four sides.
And you shall place them beneath the framework of the altar, below, and the framework shall reach halfway up the altar.
And you shall make poles for the altar, poles of rot-resistant wood, and cover them with bronze.
Put the poles through the rings. The poles shall be on both sides of the altar, for carrying it.
You shall make it hollow, constructed of planks. You shall make it according to the pattern, just as it was shown to you there on the mountain.
You shall make a courtyard for the tabernacle. On the south side, the courtyard hangings shall be of finely spun linen, a hundred cubits long on that side.
Its twenty pillars and their twenty bases shall be bronze, and their rings and capitals shall be silver.

Likewise, on the north side, the hangings shall be a hundred cubits long. Their twenty pillars shall be bronze, and their twenty bases shall be bronze; their rings, the bases of the pillars, and the bases shall be covered with silver.
Across the width of the courtyard on the west side, the hangings shall be fifty cubits long, with ten pillars and ten bases.
Across the width of the front of the courtyard, on the east side, the hangings shall be fifty cubits long, with ten pillars and ten bases.
On one side, the hangings shall be fifteen cubits high, with three pillars and three bases.
On the other side, the curtains shall be fifteen cubits high, with three pillars and three bases.
At the gate of the courtyard there shall be a curtain twenty cubits high, made of blue, purple, and spun scarlet thread and woven linen, patterned by embroiderers, with four pillars and four bases.
All the pillars around the courtyard shall be covered with silver; their capitals shall be silver, and their bases bronze.
The courtyard shall be a hundred by a hundred cubits long and fifty by fifty cubits wide, with hangings fifteen cubits high made of finely spun linen, and their bases shall be bronze.
All the furnishings of the tabernacle, all its implements, and all the pegs of the courtyard shall be bronze.
You shall command the Israelites to bring you clear, pure oil from unripe olives for lighting, so that the lamp may burn continually.

In the tabernacle of testimony, outside the curtain of the covenant, Aaron and his sons shall light it from evening until morning before the Lord. This shall be a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations among the Israelites.
You shall bring near to you your brother Aaron and his sons with him from among the Israelites, to serve me as priests: Aaron and Aaron’s sons Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
You shall make holy garments for your brother Aaron, for honor and glory.
You shall speak to all who are wise in understanding, whom I will fill with the spirit of wisdom, and they shall make holy garments for Aaron’s consecration, in which he shall serve me as a priest.

These are the kinds of garments they shall make: the breastpiece, the ephod with its shoulder pieces and chest pieces, the linen robe, the turban, and the sash. They shall make holy garments for your brother Aaron and his sons, to serve me as priests.
They shall take gold, blue and purple material, spun scarlet yarn, and fine linen.
They shall make the ephod of pure gold, blue, purple, and spun scarlet thread, and woven linen, as patterned work on the loom.
Two shoulder pieces shall be joined together and fastened on its two sides.
The worked part of the ephod that is upon it shall follow the same pattern and shall be made as part of it, of pure gold, blue, purple, and spun scarlet thread, and woven linen.
You shall take two emerald stones and engrave on them the names of the sons of Israel.
Six of their names shall be on one stone, and the other six on the second stone, according to their birth.
With the skilled workmanship of gem engravers, engrave the two stones as a seal is engraved, according to the names of the children of Israel. Make them stamped and engraved in gold.

You shall place the two stones on the shoulders of the ephod, so that the stones may be a memorial for the sons of Israel. Aaron shall carry the names of the sons of Israel before the Lord on his two shoulders as a memorial for them.
You shall make settings of pure gold.
You shall make two chains of pure gold, twisted and adorned with flowers, as braided work. You shall place the twisted chains on the two settings, beside their [?], on the front.
You shall make the breastplate of judgment with embroidered work, in the same manner as the ephod. You shall make it of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen.
You shall make it square, a span long and a span wide.
You shall set stones in it in four rows. The first row of stones shall be an emerald, a sardius, and a topaz: one row.
The second row shall be a carbuncle, a sapphire, and a jasper.
The third row shall be a ligure, an agate, and a ruby.
The fourth row shall be a hyacinth, a beryl, and an onyx. They shall be mounted in gold settings, each in its own row.
The stones shall bear the names of the sons of Israel, twelve according to their names, engraved like a seal, each with its own name, for the twelve tribes.
You shall make a breastplate with braided ends, worked like chains, of pure gold.
You shall make two gold rings for the breastplate and place the two gold rings on the two ends of the breastplate.
You shall attach the two gold chains to the two rings at the ends of the breastplate.
You shall attach the two ends of the two chains to the two fastenings and place them on the shoulder pieces of the ephod, at its front.
You shall make two gold rings and attach them to the two ends of the breastplate, on its edge facing the ephod, on the inner side.
Make two gold rings and place them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on the underside, facing one another at the joining, and its [?] above the woven work of the ephod.
They shall secure the breastplate by its rings to the rings of the ephod with a blue cord, so that it rests on the woven fabric of the ephod and the breastplate does not come loose from the ephod.
Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on the breastplate of judgment over his chest when he enters the sanctuary, as a continual remembrance before God.

You shall place the chain-work ends on the breastplate of judgment, placing them on both sides of the breastplate. You shall place the two small shields on the two shoulders of the ephod, at the front, underneath. You shall place Revelation and Truth on the breastplate of judgment, and they shall be over Aaron’s chest when he enters the sanctuary before the Lord. Aaron shall continually bear the judgments of the sons of Israel over his chest before the Lord.
You shall make a full-length robe entirely of blue.
You shall shape its collar into a circle, with a border all around, the work of a weaver, and with its joins woven into it from the outset, so that it does not tear.

Around the lower hem of the robe you shall make blossoming pomegranate-shaped ornaments of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and finely spun linen. Its appearance shall be like pomegranates, with gold bells between them all around.
A gold bell and a blossoming pomegranate-shaped ornament shall alternate around the hem of the robe.
Aaron shall wear it when he ministers, and its ringing shall sound when he enters the sanctuary before the Lord and when he comes out, so that he does not die.
You shall make the plate of pure gold and engrave on it, like the engraving of a seal: HOLINESS TO THE LORD.
You shall place it on the blue cord.

It shall be at the front of the headdress, over Aaron’s forehead. Aaron shall bear the guilt of the sacred offerings that the sons of Israel dedicate, whatever their holy gifts may be. It shall always be over Aaron’s forehead, so that they may be accepted before the Lord.
You shall make the full-length tunic of fine linen, and you shall make a turban of fine linen and a sash with embroidered work.
For Aaron’s sons, make tunics, sashes, and headdresses, for honor and glory.
You shall clothe your brother Aaron and his sons with him in these things. You shall anoint them, ordain them, and consecrate them, so that they may serve me as priests.
And you shall make linen undergarments for them to cover their private parts, extending from the waist to the thighs.

Aaron and his sons shall wear it when they enter the tent of testimony or when they approach the holy altar to minister. They must not bring sin upon themselves, lest they die. This is an everlasting ordinance for him and his descendants after him.
And this is what you shall do for them to consecrate them to serve me as priests: take one young bull from the herd and two rams without blemish.
And make unleavened loaves, unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil. You shall make them from fine wheat flour mixed with oil.
And you shall put them in one basket and bring them in the basket, together with the young bull and the two rams.
And you shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tent of testimony and wash them with water.

And you shall take the garments and dress Aaron your brother in them, putting the fringed robes over the undergarments, and the ephod and the breastplate; and you shall fasten the breastplate to the ephod.
And you shall put the turban on his head and place the holy plate on the turban.
And you shall take some of the anointing oil, pour it on his head, and anoint him.
And you shall bring his sons forward and dress them in tunics.
And you shall put sashes on them, on Aaron and his sons, and put headbands on them. They shall have an everlasting priesthood in my service, and you shall consecrate Aaron and his sons.

And you shall bring the young bull to the entrance of the tent of testimony, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the young bull’s head before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
And you shall slaughter the young bull before the Lord at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
And you shall take some of the young bull’s blood and put it on the horns of the altar with your finger, and sprinkle all the remaining blood at the base of the altar.
And you shall take all the fat covering the intestines, the lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and place them on the altar.
And you shall burn the young bull’s flesh, its hide, and its dung outside the camp, for it is a sin offering.
And you shall take the first ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram’s head.
And you shall slaughter the ram, take its blood, and pour it around the altar.
And you shall cut the ram into pieces, limb by limb, wash its entrails and legs with water, and place them on the pieces together with its head.
And you shall offer the whole ram on the altar as a burnt offering to the Lord, a pleasing aroma. It is a sacrifice to the Lord.
And you shall take the second ram, and Aaron and his sons shall lay their hands on the ram’s head.

And you shall slaughter the ram, take some of its blood, and put it on the lobe of Aaron’s right ear and on the lobe of his sons’ right ears, on the thumb of his right hand and on the big toe of his right foot, and on the lobes of his sons’ right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet. And you shall pour the blood around the altar.

And you shall take some of the blood that is on the altar and some of the anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron and on his garments, and on his sons and on his sons’ garments with him. He and his garments, and his sons and his sons’ garments with him, shall be made holy. And you shall sprinkle the ram’s blood around the altar.
And you shall take from the ram the fat, the fat tail, the fat covering the intestines, the lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh, for it is for consecration.
And take one loaf, one cake mixed with oil, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread placed before the Lord.
And you shall place all these on Aaron’s hands and on his sons’ hands, and present them as an offering before the Lord.
Take them from their hands and offer them on the altar of burnt offerings as a pleasing aroma before the Lord, for it is an offering to the Lord.
You shall take the breast from the ram of ordination that belongs to Aaron and present it as an offering before the Lord, and it shall be your portion.
You shall consecrate the breast offered as an offering and the thigh of the offering that is presented, and whatever is taken from the ram of ordination belonging to Aaron and his sons.

It shall belong to Aaron and his sons as a perpetual ordinance from the Israelites, for it is their allotted portion. It shall be an offering from the Israelites, from their sacrifices of well-being, their offering to the Lord.
The holy robe that belongs to Aaron shall belong to his sons after him, so that they may be anointed in it and ordained in it.
The priest from among his sons who succeeds him, who enters the tent of testimony to minister in the holy place, shall wear it for seven days.
You shall take the ram of ordination and boil its meat in a holy place.
Aaron and his sons shall eat the meat of the ram and the [?] that are in the basket there, at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
They shall eat those things by which they were sanctified when they were ordained and consecrated. No outsider shall eat any of them, for they are holy.
If any of the meat of the ordination sacrifice or any of the bread remains until morning, you shall burn the remainder with fire. It shall not be eaten, for it is holy to the Lord.
You shall do this for Aaron and his sons according to everything I have commanded you. For seven days you shall ordain them.
You shall offer the bull as a sin offering on the day of purification. You shall purify the altar when you make purification upon it, and you shall anoint it to consecrate it.
For seven days you shall purify the altar and consecrate it. The altar shall be most holy; everything that touches the altar shall become holy.
This is what you shall offer on the altar: two unblemished year-old lambs each day upon the altar continually, for it is a continual offering.
You shall offer one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer the second lamb in the evening.
With one lamb, offer a tenth measure of fine flour mixed with a quarter of a measure of pressed oil, and a drink offering of a quarter of a measure of wine.
You shall offer the second lamb in the evening. You shall offer it with the same sacrifice and drink offering as in the morning, as a pleasing fragrance, an offering to the Lord.
It shall be a continual sacrifice throughout your generations at the entrance of the tent of testimony before the Lord, through which I will make myself known to you there, to speak with you.
I will meet the children of Israel there, and I will be sanctified by my glory.
I will consecrate the tent of testimony and the altar, and I will consecrate Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests.
I will be called upon among the Israelites, and I will be their God.
They shall know that I am the Lord their God, who brought them out of the land of the Egyptians to be called upon by them and to be the Lord their God.
You shall make an altar for burning incense from wood that does not decay.
You shall make it one cubit long and one cubit wide. It shall be square, and its height shall be two cubits. Its horns shall be of one piece with it.
Overlay it with pure gold—its grating, its sides all around, and its horns—and make a gold molding around it.
You shall make two rings of pure gold beneath the molding around it, on its two sides. You shall make them at its two corners, and they shall be holders for the poles used to carry it.
You shall make the poles from wood that does not decay and overlay them with gold.
You shall place it opposite the curtain that is before the ark of testimony, opposite the testimony that is beside the testimony, through which I will appear to you there.
Aaron shall put prepared incense, finely ground, on it every morning. When he tends the lamps, he shall burn incense on it.
When Aaron lights the lamps in the evening, he shall burn incense on it as a continual daily offering before the Lord throughout their generations.
You shall not offer foreign incense, offerings of produce, or sacrifices on it, and you shall not present offerings on it.

Once a year Aaron shall make atonement on its horns with the blood of the sin offering for purification and atonement. Once a year he shall purify it throughout their generations, for it is most holy to the Lord.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
When you count the Israelites in their census, each shall give the Lord a ransom for his life when they are counted, so that no death occurs among them during their census.

This is what everyone who passes through the census shall give: half a didrachm according to the sanctuary didrachm. The didrachm is twenty obols, and half a didrachm shall be the contribution to the Lord.
Everyone who passes through the census, from twenty years old and upward, shall give the contribution to the Lord.
The rich shall not give more, and the poor shall not give less than half a didrachm when giving the contribution to the Lord from the Israelites, to make atonement for your lives.

You shall take the silver contribution from the Israelites and give it for the work of the tent of testimony. It shall be a memorial for the Israelites before the Lord, to make atonement for their lives.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Make a bronze basin with a bronze base for washing, and place it between the tent of testimony and the altar, and put water in it.
Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and feet with water from it.
When they enter the tent of testimony, they shall wash with water so that they do not die, or when they approach the altar to serve and to offer burnt offerings to the Lord.
They shall wash their hands and feet so that they do not die. This shall be an everlasting statute for them, for him and his descendants after him.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Take for yourself fragrant spices: five hundred shekels of choice myrrh blossoms, half that amount of fragrant cinnamon—two hundred and fifty—and two hundred and fifty of fragrant calamus,
and five hundred shekels of iris according to the sanctuary measure, and one hin of olive oil.
You shall make these into holy anointing oil, oil compounded according to the perfumers’ art. It shall be holy anointing oil.
With it you shall anoint the tent of testimony and the ark of testimony,
the table and all its utensils, the lampstand and all its utensils, and the altar of incense,
the altar of burnt offerings and all its utensils, and the basin and its base.
You shall consecrate them, and they shall be most holy. Everything that touches them shall become holy.
You shall anoint Aaron and his sons and consecrate them to serve me as priests.
You shall speak to the Israelites and say, ‘This shall be your holy anointing oil throughout your generations.
It shall not be applied to a human body, and you shall not make any like it for yourselves according to this preparation, for it is holy and shall be holy to you.
Whoever makes any like it, or gives any of it to an outsider, shall be cut off from his people.’
The Lord said to Moses, ‘Take for yourself fragrant spices: stacte, onycha, fragrant galbanum, and pure frankincense. They shall be in equal amounts.’
And you shall make it into compounded incense, the work of perfumers, a fragrant preparation, pure and holy.
And you shall grind some of it finely and place some of it before the testimony in the tent of testimony, where I will appear to you. The incense that you make shall be most holy to you.
Do not make incense for yourselves according to that preparation, for it shall be holy to the Lord for you.
Anyone who makes something like it in order to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
Look, I have called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.
And I have filled him with the divine Spirit, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge of every kind of work,
to understand and devise designs, to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
in blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn, and in setting stones to complete the work, and to do woodworking, performing every kind of work.

And look, I have appointed him and Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan. And I have put wisdom into the heart of every skilled person, so that they may make everything I have commanded you:
the tent of testimony, the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat upon it, all the equipment of the tent, and the places of sacrifice;
the table and all its utensils, the holy lampstand and all its utensils, and the incense altar;
the altar of burnt offerings and all its utensils, and the basin and its stand;
the robes for service, the holy garments of Aaron the priest, and the robes of his sons for serving me as priests;
and the anointing oil and the fragrant incense for the sanctuary. You shall make everything I have commanded you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

And you shall speak to the Israelites and say, “Be careful to keep my Sabbaths, for this is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, so that you may know that I am the Lord who makes you holy.”
Keep the Sabbaths, for the Sabbath is holy to the Lord and to you. Whoever profanes it shall be put to death. Whoever does any work on it shall be cut off from among his people.
For six days you shall work, but on the seventh day there shall be a Sabbath of rest, holy to the Lord. Anyone who does work on the Sabbath day shall surely be put to death.
And the Israelites shall keep the Sabbaths, observing them throughout your generations as an everlasting covenant.
It is my everlasting sign between me and the Israelites, for in six days the Lord made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he ceased and rested.
And when he had finished speaking on Mount Sinai, he gave Moses the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written with the finger of God.

When the people saw that Moses was taking a long time to come down from the mountain, they gathered around Aaron and said to him, “Come, make us gods who will lead us, for we do not know what has happened to this man Moses, who brought us out of Egypt.”
And Aaron said to them, “Take the gold earrings from the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.”
And all the people took the gold earrings from their ears and brought them to Aaron.
And he received them from their hands and cast the gold using an engraving tool, making a cast calf. And they said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
And when Aaron saw it, he built an altar before it. Aaron made a proclamation and said, “Tomorrow is a feast to the Lord.”
And early the next morning he offered burnt offerings and presented peace offerings. The people sat down to eat and drink, and rose up to play.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said, “Go down from here quickly, for your people, whom you brought out of the land of Egypt, have acted lawlessly.”

They quickly turned aside from the way you commanded them. They made themselves a cast calf, bowed down to it, sacrificed to it, and said, “These are your gods, Israel, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.”
And the Lord said to Moses, “I have seen this people, and look, they are a stiff-necked people.”
Now leave me alone, and in my fierce anger against them I will destroy them and make you into a great nation.
Moses pleaded before the Lord his God and said, “Why, Lord, are you fiercely angry with your people, whom you brought out of the land of the Egyptians with great power and an uplifted arm?

The Egyptians might say, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to slaughter them in the mountains and wipe them off the earth.’ Turn away from your fierce anger and relent from bringing harm upon your people.

Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, your servants, to whom you swore by yourself. You spoke with them and said, ‘I will greatly multiply your offspring, making them as numerous as the stars of heaven.’ And they will possess forever all that land which you promised to give to their offspring.”
And the Lord relented from the harm he had said he would bring upon his people.
Moses turned and came down from the mountain, with the two tablets of the testimony in his hands—stone tablets inscribed on both sides, written on one side and the other.
The tablets were the work of God, and the writing was God's writing, engraved on the tablets.
When Joshua heard the sound of the people shouting, he said to Moses, “There is the sound of war in the camp.”
He said, “It is not the sound of warriors displaying strength, nor the cry of warriors displaying courage; rather, I hear the sound of people made senseless by wine.”
When he approached the camp and saw the calf and the dancers, Moses became fiercely angry. He threw the two tablets from his hands and shattered them at the foot of the mountain.
He took the calf they had made, burned it with fire, ground it finely, scattered it over the water, and made the Israelites drink it.
Moses said to Aaron, “What did this people do to you, that you brought this terrible sin upon them?”
Aaron said to Moses, “Do not be fiercely angry, my lord, for you yourself know the recklessness of this people.
They said, ‘Make us gods who will lead us, because we do not know what has happened to that man Moses, who brought us out of Egypt.’
I said to them, ‘If anyone has gold, take it off and bring it.’ They gave it to me, and I threw it into the fire, and this calf came out.”
Moses saw that the people had gone astray, for Aaron had led them astray, leaving them to be trampled by their enemies.
Moses stood at the gate of the camp and said, “Whoever belongs to the Lord, come to me.” All the sons of Levi gathered around him.

He said to them, “Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Each of you strap his sword to his thigh. Go back and forth from gate to gate through this camp, and each of you kill his brother, his companion, and his neighbor.”
The sons of Levi did as Moses said, and about three thousand men from among the people fell that day.
Moses said to them, “Consecrate yourselves today to the Lord, each against his own son and each against his own brother, so that he may bestow a blessing upon you today.”
The next day, Moses said to the people, “You have committed this great sin. But now I will go up to God, so that I may make atonement for your sins.”
Moses returned to the Lord and said, “I beg you, Lord: this people has committed a dreadful sin and made gods of gold for themselves.
Now, if you will forgive their sins, forgive them; but if not, erase me from your book in which you have written me.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Whoever has sinned before me, I will erase from my book.
But now go down and lead this people to the place I told you about. See, my angel will go before you. But on the day when I call them to account, I will bring their sins upon them.”
And the Lord struck the people because they had made the calf that Aaron made.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Go up from here, you and your people whom you brought out of the land of the Egyptians, to the land that I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to give, saying, ‘I will give it to your descendants.’”
“And I will send my angel before you, and he will drive out the Canaanites, the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites.
And he will bring you into a land flowing with milk and honey. But I will not go up with you, because the people are stiff-necked, lest I destroy you on the way.”
When the people heard this bad news, they went into mourning, and no one put on any ornaments.

And the Lord said to Moses, “Say to the children of Israel, ‘You are a stiff-necked people. Beware, lest I strike you with yet another blow and destroy you. Now strip off your splendid garments and remove your ornaments, and I will show you what I will do to you.’”
The children of Israel stripped off their ornaments and their robes at Mount Horeb.

And Moses took his tent and pitched it outside the camp, apart from the camp, and it was called the Tent of Testimony. Everyone who sought anything from the Lord would go out to the Tent of Testimony outside the camp.
Whenever Moses went to the tent, all the people stood watching, each at the entrance of his own tent, and watched Moses until he went into the tent.
Whenever Moses entered the tent, the pillar of cloud would descend and stand at the entrance of the tent, and the Lord would speak with Moses.
All the people would see the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance of the tent, and all the people would stand up and bow down, each at the entrance of his own tent.
And the Lord would speak with Moses face to face, as someone speaks with his friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his attendant Joshua son of Nun would not leave the tent.

And Moses said to the Lord, “Look, you tell me, ‘Bring up these people,’ but you have not shown me whom you will send with me. And you have said to me, ‘I know you above all others, and you have favor with me.’

Now, if I have found favor before you, show yourself to me clearly, so that I may know how I have found favor before you, and so that I may know that these people of yours will become a great nation.”
And he said, “I myself will go before you and settle you.”
And Moses said to him, “If you yourself will not go with us, do not bring us up from here.
And how will it be known that I and your people have truly found favor before you? Rather, by your going with us, I and your people will be glorified above all the nations on the earth.”
And the Lord said to Moses, “I will also do this thing that you have asked, because you have found favor before me, and I know you above all others.”
And Moses said, “Show me your glory.”

And he said, “I will pass before you in my glory, and I will call on the name of the Lord before you. I will have mercy on whomever I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whomever I have compassion.”
And he said, “You cannot see my face, because no one can see my face and live.
The Lord said, “Here is a place before me, and you shall stand on the rock.”
When my glory passes by, I will put you in a cleft of the rock and cover you with my hand until I have passed by.
Then I will lift my hand away from you, and you will see my back, but my face will not be visible to you.”

And the Lord said to Moses, “Cut two stone tablets for yourself like the first tablets, and come up to me on the mountain. I will write on the tablets the words that were on the first tablets, which you broke.
Be ready for tomorrow, and come up in the morning to Mount Sinai, and wait for me there on the summit of the mountain.”
No one is to go up with you, and no one is to appear anywhere on the mountain. Cattle and sheep are not to graze near the mountain.
He cut two stone tablets like the first ones. Moses rose early in the morning and went up Mount Sinai, as the Lord had commanded him, and Moses took the two stone tablets with him.
The Lord came down in a cloud and stood there before him, and called upon the name of the Lord.
The Lord passed before him and proclaimed, “The Lord God, compassionate and merciful, patient, abundant in mercy and true,

who preserves righteousness and shows mercy to a thousand generations, takes away lawlessness, wrongdoing, and sins, but does not acquit the guilty, bringing the lawlessness of fathers upon their children and their children’s children, to the third and fourth generations.”
Moses hurried to bow down to the ground in worship and said,
“If I have found favor before you, Lord, let the Lord go with us, for this people is stubborn. Take away our lawlessness and our sins, and let us be yours.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Look, I am making a covenant with you. Before all your people I will perform wonders that have never been done anywhere on earth or among any nations. All the people among whom you live will see the works of the Lord, for the things I will do for you will be astonishing.
Be careful to observe everything that I command you today. Look, I am driving out before you the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.
Take care not to make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land into which you are entering, lest it become a stumbling block for you.
You must demolish their altars, smash their pillars, cut down their sacred groves, and burn the carved images of their gods with fire.
Do not bow down to foreign gods, for the Lord God’s name is Jealous; he is a jealous God.
Lest they make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, prostitute themselves by following their gods, sacrifice to their gods, and invite you, and you eat from their sacrifices.

And you take their daughters for your sons and give your daughters to their sons, and your daughters prostitute themselves by following them and cause your sons to prostitute themselves by following their gods.
Do not make cast-metal gods for yourself.

Keep the Feast of Unleavened Bread. For seven days you must eat unleavened bread, as I commanded you, at its appointed time in the month of the early crops, for in the month of the early crops you came out of Egypt.
Every male that opens the womb shall be mine, and every male firstborn of your livestock, the firstborn of cattle and the firstborn of sheep.
Redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb. If you do not redeem it, pay its price. Redeem all the firstborn of your sons, and they must not appear before me empty-handed.
Work for six days, and rest on the seventh day. Rest even during sowing and harvest.
Celebrate the Festival of Weeks for me at the beginning of the wheat harvest, and the festival of gathering the crops in the middle of the year.
Three times a year every male child of yours must appear before the Lord, the God of Israel.
For I will drive out the nations before you and enlarge your borders, and no one will covet your land when you go up to appear before the Lord your God three times a year.
Do not offer the blood of my sacrifices with leavened bread, and do not let the sacrifice of the Passover feast remain until morning.
Bring the first produce of your land to the house of the Lord your God. Do not boil a lamb in its mother’s milk.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Write down these words for yourself, for according to these words I will make a covenant with you and with me.”
Moses was before the Lord for forty days and forty nights. He ate no bread and drank no water, and he wrote on the tablets the words of the covenant, the Ten Commandments.
As Moses came down from Mount Sinai, the two tablets of the covenant were in his hands. As he came down from the mountain, Moses did not know that his face had become radiant from speaking with him.
Aaron and all the Israelites saw Moses, and his face was radiant, and they were afraid to approach him.
Moses called to them, and Aaron and all the leaders of the people returned to him, and Moses spoke with them.
Then all the Israelites approached him, and he told them everything that the Lord had said to him on Mount Sinai.
When he finished speaking with them, he put a veil over his face.
Whenever Moses went in before the Lord to speak with him, he removed the veil until he came out again. When he came out, he told all the Israelites everything that the Lord had commanded him.
The Israelites saw Moses’ face, for his face was radiant. Moses would put the veil over his face until he went in again to speak with him.
Moses assembled the whole congregation of the Israelites and said to them, “These are the things that the Lord has said to do:
For six days you shall work, but on the seventh day you shall rest. It is a holy Sabbath, a rest for the Lord. Anyone who works on it shall be put to death.
No fire shall be lit in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day, for I am the Lord.”
Moses spoke to the whole congregation of the Israelites and said, “This is the command that the Lord gave, saying:
Take from among yourselves a contribution for the Lord. Let everyone whose heart is willing bring an offering to the Lord: gold, silver, bronze,
blue and purple yarn, double-spun scarlet yarn, spun fine linen, and goats’ hair,
rams’ skins dyed red, skins dyed blue, and wood that does not rot,
oil for lighting, spices for the anointing oil, and spices for the incense mixture,
carnelian stones, emerald stones, and stones for engraving for the ephod and the ankle-length robe.
Let everyone among you who is skilled in heart come and make everything that the Lord has commanded:
the tabernacle, its curtains, its coverings, its clasps, its boards, its crossbars, its pillars, and its bases,
the ark of the testimony, its poles, the atonement cover, the veil, the curtain of the courtyard, its pillars, the emerald stones, the spices, and the anointing oil,
the table and all its utensils, the coverings of the table, its poles, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence,
the lampstand for lighting, all its utensils, its lamps, and the oil for lighting,
the incense altar, its poles, the anointing oil, the incense mixture, and the curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle,
the altar of burnt offerings, its bronze grating, its poles, all its utensils, the basin, and its base,
the curtain of the courtyard, its pillars, its bases, and the screen for the entrance of the courtyard,
and the pegs of the tabernacle, the pegs of the courtyard, and their ropes;
and the garments for serving in the sanctuary, the holy garments of Aaron the priest, and the priestly garments of Aaron’s sons.
Then the whole assembly of the Israelites departed from Moses.

Each brought as his heart moved him, and all whose spirits were willing brought offerings to the Lord for all the work of the tabernacle of testimony, for all its materials, and for all the holy garments.

The men brought from the women, everyone as his mind moved him, precious stones, earrings, rings, hair ornaments, breast ornaments, and every kind of gold object. All the men who had gold brought offerings of gold to the Lord.
Everyone who had blue, purple, or spun scarlet yarn, fine linen, goats’ hair, rams’ skins dyed red, or skins dyed blue brought them.
Everyone who offered silver or bronze brought the offerings to the Lord, and everyone who had rot-resistant wood brought it for all the work on the furnishings.
Every woman skilled in mind spun with her own hands and brought the spun blue and purple yarn, the scarlet-dyed yarn, and the fine linen.
All the women whose minds moved them spun the goats’ hair skillfully.
The leaders brought emeralds and stones to be used for the ephod and the breastplate,
and the ingredients for the incense, the oil for lighting, and the anointing oil.
Every man and woman whose mind moved them came to carry out all the work that the Lord had commanded through Moses. The Israelites brought their offerings to the Lord.
Moses said to the Israelites, “See, God has called by name Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah.
He has filled him with the divine Spirit, with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in everything,
for every kind of work: to devise skillful designs and to work in gold, silver, and bronze,
to engrave stones and work in wood, and to carry out every kind of skilled work.
He has put wisdom in his heart to instruct others, and also in the heart of Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

He has filled them with wisdom of mind to understand how to carry out all the work of the sanctuary: weaving, embroidery with blue, purple, scarlet-dyed yarn, and fine linen, and every kind of skilled work done by designers.”

Bezalel and Oholiab, and every man skilled in mind to whom the Lord had given wisdom and knowledge to understand how to carry out all the work of furnishing the sanctuary, did everything just as the Lord had commanded.
Moses called Bezalel and Oholiab and everyone who had wisdom in his heart, in whose hearts God had placed understanding—all whose minds willingly moved them to approach the work and complete it.

They received from Moses all the offerings that the Israelites had brought to carry out all the work of furnishing the sanctuary. They continued receiving offerings from those who brought them, morning after morning.
All the skilled workers who were doing the work of the sanctuary came, each from the particular work he was doing.
They spoke to Moses and said, “The people are bringing far more than is needed for the materials required for the work that God commanded to be done.”
Moses ordered a proclamation to be made in the camp, saying, “Let neither man nor woman make anything more as an offering for the sanctuary.” Then the people were restrained from bringing more.
They brought what they had made for all the construction work, to carry it out, and then they stopped.
All those skilled in heart among the workers made the tabernacle with ten curtains of finely spun linen, blue, purple, and double-dyed scarlet, with cherubim worked into the fabric.
The length of each curtain was twenty-eight cubits, and the width of each curtain was four cubits. All the curtains had the same measurements.
He joined the five curtains to the other five curtains, and also joined the five curtains to another five.
He made blue loops along the edge of one curtain, on the side where they were joined. Likewise, he made them along the edge of the outermost curtain of the second set.
He made fifty loops on one curtain and fifty loops along the side of the curtain of the second set, so that the individual loops could be joined to one another.
He made fifty gold clasps and joined the curtains to one another with the clasps, so that the tabernacle became one whole.
He made curtains of haircloth to cover the tabernacle. He made eleven curtains.
The length of each curtain was thirty cubits, and the width of each curtain was four cubits. All eleven curtains had the same measurements.
He joined the five curtains together and the six curtains together.
He made fifty loops along the edge of the curtain at the junction of the sets, and he made another fifty loops along the edge of the curtain of the second set.
He made fifty bronze clasps and joined the tabernacle together so that it would be one.
He made the coverings of the tabernacle from ram skins dyed red, and the outer coverings above them from blue material.
He made the two upright pillars of the tabernacle from rot-resistant wood.
The length of each pillar was ten cubits, and the thickness and width of each pillar were one and a half cubits.
Each pillar had two tenons joined to one another. He made all the pillars of the tabernacle in the same way.
He made the pillars of the tabernacle: twenty pillars on the south side,
and forty silver bases for the twenty pillars, two bases for one pillar on its two sides, and two bases for another pillar on its two sides.
On the second side of the tabernacle, toward the north, he made twenty pillars
and forty silver bases, two bases for one pillar and two bases for another pillar.
At the rear of the tabernacle, toward the west, he made six pillars.
He made two pillars for the corners of the tabernacle at the rear.
They were joined together below, and in the same way they were joined together at the top into one joint. He did the same for both pillars at the corners.
There were eight pillars, and their bases were silver: sixteen bases, two bases for one pillar and two bases for one pillar.
He made bars of rot-resistant wood, five for one upright on one side of the tabernacle.
And five more crossbars for the other pillar on the second side of the tabernacle, and five crossbars for the other pillar at the rear of the tabernacle, toward the west.
He made the middle crossbar pass through the middle of the pillars from one side to the other.
He overlaid the two pillars with gold and made their two rings of gold, through which the crossbars would pass. He overlaid the crossbars with gold.
He made a veil of blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and woven fine linen. He made it as woven work, with a cherub.
And he placed it on four pillars of decay-resistant wood overlaid with gold. Their capitals were gold, and their four bases were silver.
And he made the curtain for the entrance of the tent of testimony from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn and finely woven linen, woven work with a cherub.
And he made its five pillars and their rings, and overlaid their capitals with gold. Their five bases were bronze.
And Bezalel made the ark from decay-resistant wood, two and a half cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one and a half cubits high.
And he overlaid it with pure gold inside and outside, and made a gold molding around it.
And he cast four gold rings for it at its four corners, two rings on one side and two rings on the other side, and fittings for the poles.
And he made poles from decay-resistant wood and overlaid them with gold.
And they inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the ark to carry it with them.
And they made the atonement cover above the ark from pure gold, two and a half cubits long and one and a half cubits wide.
And he made two gold cherubim; he fashioned them as hammered work at the two sides of the atonement cover.
One cherub was at one end of the atonement cover, and one cherub was at the other end of the atonement cover. He made the two cherubim from the cover itself, at its two ends.
And the cherubim spread their wings above, overshadowing the atonement cover with their wings. The faces of the cherubim faced one another over the atonement cover.

And he made the table of presentation from pure gold, and cast four gold rings for it, two on one side and two on the other side, and carrying poles to carry it with. And he made the carrying poles of the ark and of the table from decay-resistant wood and overlaid them with gold. The table was two cubits long, one and a half cubits wide, and one and a half cubits high.
And he overlaid it with pure gold and made a gold molding around it.
He made a border a handbreadth wide all around it, and made gold moldings all around its border.
And he made four gold rings for it and placed the rings at the four corners by its four feet.
The rings were beneath the rim, as fittings for the poles for carrying the table.
And he made two poles from decay-resistant wood and overlaid them with gold, for carrying the table.
And he made the utensils of the table—its incense dishes, its blood bowls, its cups, and its offering vessels with which offerings were to be made—from pure gold.

And he made the lampstand for giving light from cast gold: its shaft and its branches on its two sides. From the branches came offshoots separated from one another, three on one side and three on the other, matching one another. Their lamp holders, which were at the ends, had nut-shaped decorations, formed separately [?]. And he made the supports on them so that the lamps would rest upon them, and the seventh support at the top of the lamp holder, above the very top of the shaft, cast entirely from gold. And he made the seven lamps upon it of gold, its tongs of gold, and its trimming tools of gold. He fashioned the lampstand from pure gold as hammered work, its shaft, its branches, its cup-shaped pieces, its knobs, and its lilies, all from the same piece.
Six branches extended from its sides: three branches from one side of the lampstand and three branches from the other side of the lampstand.

Three nut-decorated, cup-shaped ornaments were fashioned on one branch, with a knob and a lily, and three nut-decorated, cup-shaped ornaments on another branch, with a knob and a lily. So it was for all six branches extending from the lampstand.
On the shaft of the lampstand were four nut-decorated, cup-shaped ornaments, with its knobs and lilies.
A knob beneath each pair of branches was of one piece with it, for all six branches extending from it.
Their knobs and their branches were of one piece with it, all worked from a single piece of pure gold.
He made its seven lamps, its tongs, and its trimmers of pure gold.
He made it and all its utensils from one talent of pure gold.
He made the gold-covered altar of rot-resistant wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide, square, and three cubits high. Its horns were of one piece with it.
He covered it with pure gold—its top, its sides all around, and its horns—and made a gold molding around it.
He made two gold rings beneath its molding, on its sides, on both sides, as holders for the poles used to carry it.
He made the poles of rot-resistant wood and covered them with gold.
He made the holy anointing oil and the preparation of incense, the pure work of perfumers.

He made the bronze-covered altar from the bronze censers that had been in the hands of the men who rebelled with Korah's congregation. It was made of rot-resistant wood, five cubits long and five cubits wide, square, and three cubits high.
He also made its horns on its four corners. Its horns were of one piece with it, and he covered them with bronze.
He made all the altar's utensils: the bases, the shovel, the basins, the meat forks, and the censers. He made all its utensils of bronze.
He made the altar's grates of bronze meshwork from the censers, underneath, extending halfway up.
He put four bronze rings on the four sides of the altar's grate as holders for the carrying bars.
He made the poles of rot-resistant wood and covered them with bronze.
They inserted the poles into the rings on the sides of the table to carry the table with them. He made it entirely of boards.
He made the bronze basin and its bronze base from the mirrors of the women who had taken vows and observed fasts at the entrance to the tent of testimony, on the day when he set up the tent.
He made the courtyard facing south, and the courtyard's hanging of finely spun linen, a hundred by a hundred.
Their pillars were twenty, and their bronze bases twenty. The ornaments of the pillars and their capitals were silver.
On the north side it was a hundred by a hundred. Their pillars were twenty, and their bronze bases twenty. The ornaments of the pillars and their bands were silver.
On the west side the hangings were fifty cubits long. Their pillars were ten, and their bases ten. The ornaments of the pillars and their bands were silver.
On the east side it was fifty cubits long.
The hangings on one flank were fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
On the other flank, beside the courtyard entrance, the hangings were fifteen cubits long, with three pillars and three bases.
All the hangings around the courtyard of the tabernacle were of spun fine linen.

Their bases were bronze, and the bands of the pillars and their hooks were silver. Their capitals were overlaid with silver, and the pillars—all the pillars of the courtyard—were overlaid with silver.

The curtain for the courtyard entrance was embroidered work of blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and twisted fine linen, twenty cubits long and fifteen cubits high, with its width matching the hangings of the courtyard.
Their four pillars had four bronze bases, silver hooks, and capitals overlaid with silver.
All the pegs around the courtyard and the tabernacle were bronze.
This was the account of the tabernacle of the testimony, as Moses was commanded to organize the service of the Levites under Ithamar, son of Aaron the priest.
Bezalel, son of Uri, son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, did as the Lord commanded Moses.
After him was Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, who was skilled in weaving, needlework, and embroidery in blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and twisted fine linen.
All the gold used in the work, for all the work of the sanctuary, amounted to twenty-nine talents and seven hundred thirty shekels of donated gold, according to the sanctuary shekel.
The silver offerings from the men of the people who passed through the census amounted to one hundred talents and one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.

One drachma per person, half a shekel according to the sanctuary shekel, was collected from everyone who passed through the census, from twenty years old and upward: six hundred three thousand five hundred fifty people.
The one hundred talents of silver were used to cast the hundred capitals of the tabernacle and the capitals for the curtain: one hundred talents for one hundred capitals, one talent per capital.
He used the one thousand seven hundred seventy-five shekels to make hooks for the pillars, overlaid their capitals with gold, and adorned them.
The donated bronze amounted to seventy talents and two thousand four hundred shekels.
From it he made the bases for the entrance of the tabernacle of the testimony, the bronze altar, the bronze stand for the altar, and all the utensils of the altar,
and the bases around the courtyard, the bases for the courtyard entrance, all the pegs of the tabernacle, all the pegs around the courtyard, and the remaining blue, purple, and spun scarlet yarn.
He made the garments for service, to serve in the sanctuary in them, and he made the holy garments for Aaron the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the ephod of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and twisted fine linen.
They cut the gold plates into threads to weave them into the blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and twisted fine linen.
They made it as woven work for the ephod, joining its two sides together and interweaving the woven work into a single piece.
They made it from the same material, matching its workmanship, of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and twisted fine linen, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He prepared the two emerald stones, bordered and set in gold, engraved and fitted with the names of the sons of Israel carved as on a seal.
He fastened them on the shoulders of the ephod as memorial stones for the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Moses.
He made the breastpiece as embroidered woven work, matching the workmanship of the ephod, of gold, blue, purple, spun scarlet yarn, and twisted fine linen.
He made the breastpiece square and doubled, a span long and a span wide.
He wove into it settings for four rows of stones. The first row was sardius, topaz, and emerald—one row.
The second row was carbuncle, sapphire, and jasper.
The third row was ruby, [?], and agate.
The fourth row was chrysolite, onyx, and beryl, enclosed and set in gold.
The stones corresponded to the names of the sons of Israel: there were twelve, inscribed with their names and engraved individually with the names of the twelve tribes.
They made dangling chains for the breastpiece, braided work of pure gold, upon the two rings.
They made two gold plaques and two gold rings, and put the two gold rings at the two ends of the breastpiece.
They put the dangling chains on the two rings at the two sides of the breastpiece.
At the two connections they placed the two dangling chains upon the two plaques, and placed these upon the shoulders of the ephod, facing outward on its front.
They made two gold rings and placed them on the two sides, at the ends of the breastpiece, at the upper part of the back of the ephod, on its underside.
They made two gold rings and placed them on the two shoulder pieces of the ephod, on its lower side, at its front, by the upper join of the woven ephod.

They fastened the breastpiece by its rings to the rings of the ephod, joining them together with braided blue cords at the woven portion of the ephod, so that the breastpiece would not come loose from the ephod, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the robes worn beneath the ephod, woven entirely of blue.
The neck openings of the robes were in the middle of the woven fabric itself, with a woven border around each opening so that it would not tear.
Along the hems of the robes they made ornaments like blossoming pomegranates, of blue, purple, spun scarlet, and woven fine linen.
They made bells of pure gold and placed the bells among the pomegranate-shaped ornaments all around the hems of the robes.
Among the pomegranate-shaped ornaments were gold bells: a pomegranate, a bell, and a pomegranate, all around the hems of the robes, for service in worship, as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made woven linen tunics for Aaron and his sons.
And the headbands of fine linen, the turban of fine linen, and the trousers of woven fine linen.
And their sashes of woven fine linen, blue, purple, and spun scarlet, embroidered work, just as the Lord commanded Moses.
They made the gold plate, the sacred dedication, of pure gold, and inscribed on it engraved lettering like a seal: HOLY TO THE LORD.
They attached it with a blue ribbon so that it would sit upon the upper part of the turban, just as the Lord commanded Moses.

All the work on the tabernacle, the tent of testimony, was completed. The Israelites did everything just as the Lord had commanded Moses. From the gold left over from the offerings, they made utensils with which to serve before the Lord.
They brought the garments to Moses at the tabernacle, together with the tent and all its furnishings, its pins, its boards, its bars, its pillars, and its bases;
the skins, the ram hides dyed red, the blue hides, and the screening curtain;
the ark of the covenant, its carrying poles, and the atonement cover;
the table set out before the Lord, all its utensils, and the bread of the Presence.
And the holy lampstand, its lamp holders, the lamps for burning, all its equipment, and the oil for lighting.
And the gold altar, the anointing oil, the compounded incense, the curtains of the entrance, and the tabernacle.
And the bronze altar, its carrying poles, all its equipment, the basin, and its base.

And the hangings of the courtyard, its pillars and their bases, the curtain for the entrance of the tabernacle and for the entrance of the courtyard, its cords and its pegs, and all the equipment of the tabernacle, the tent of testimony.
And the garments for service in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons to serve as priests.
The Israelites made all the furnishings according to everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
Moses inspected all the work, and it had been done according to the pattern. They had done it just as the Lord had commanded Moses, and Moses blessed them.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
On the first day of the first month, you shall set up the tabernacle, the tent of testimony.
You shall place the ark of testimony there and screen the ark with the curtain.
You shall bring the table inside and arrange the bread on it. You shall bring the lampstand inside and place its lamp holders on it.
You shall place the gold altar for burning incense before the ark of testimony, and hang the screening curtain at the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony.
You shall place the altar of burnt offerings at the entrance of the tabernacle, the tent of testimony. You shall anoint the tabernacle all around and consecrate everything within it on every side.
You shall place the basin between the tabernacle of testimony and the altar, and put water in it.
You shall anoint the courtyard all around and hang the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard.
You shall take the anointing oil and anoint the tabernacle and everything in it. You shall consecrate it and all its equipment, and they shall be holy.
You shall anoint the altar of burnt offerings and all its equipment, and consecrate the altar. The altar shall be most holy.
You shall anoint the basin and its base and consecrate it.
You shall bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the tabernacle of testimony and wash them with water.
You shall clothe Aaron in the holy robe, anoint him, and consecrate him, so that he may serve me as priest.
You shall bring his sons forward and clothe them in robes.
You shall anoint them just as you anointed their father, so that they may serve me as priests. Their anointing shall establish an everlasting priesthood for them throughout their generations.
Moses did everything that the Lord had commanded him; that is what he did.
The tabernacle was set up on the first day of the first month in the second year after their departure from the land of the Egyptians.
Moses set up the tabernacle, placed its bases, erected its pillars, put their capitals on top, and extended its crossbars.
He spread the roof covering over the tabernacle, put the tabernacle's coverings over it, and arranged its outer coverings, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He took the testimony and placed it inside the ark. He placed the poles beneath the ark and put the atonement cover on top of the ark.
He brought the ark inside the tabernacle, hung the screening curtain, and screened the ark of testimony, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the table in the tent of testimony, on the north side of the tent, outside the tent’s curtain.
He arranged the bread of the Presence on it before the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the lampstand in the tent of testimony, opposite the table, on the south side of the tent.
He placed the lamps on it before the Lord, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the golden altar in the tent of testimony, in front of the curtain.
He burned some of the prepared incense on it, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He hung the screen at the entrance of the tent.
He placed the altar of burnt offerings at the entrance of the tent, the dwelling of testimony, and offered burnt offerings and sacrifices on it, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He placed the basin between the tent of testimony and the altar and put water in it,
so that Moses, Aaron, and his sons could wash their hands and feet with water from it.
Whenever they entered the tent of testimony or approached the altar to minister, they washed with water from it, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
He set up the courtyard around the tent and the altar and hung the screen at the entrance of the courtyard. And Moses completed all the work.
The cloud covered the tent of testimony, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Moses could not enter the tent of testimony because the cloud covered it, and the tent was filled with the glory of the Lord.
Whenever the cloud rose from the tent, the Israelites set out with all their households.
But if the cloud did not rise, they did not set out until the day it rose.
For the cloud of the Lord was over the tent by day, and fire was over it by night, in the sight of the whole house of Israel throughout all their journeys.
